summary: PolyPid reports positive SHIELD II results, but the registered primary endpoint and incision-defined population differ from broad SSI-prevention claims. Applicability to the proposed colorectal-surgery indication remains a substantive question.
pivotalQuestion: Do the results support SSI prevention across the proposed colorectal-surgery population, beyond the registered composite endpoint in patients with incisions over 20 cm?

factors.rationale: PolyPid reports endpoints met and a 60% relative SSI reduction. The registered primary endpoint is a 30-day composite of SSI, re-intervention or death in patients with incisions over 20 cm.
The supplied summaries provide no interpretable adverse-event or tolerability results.
No product-linked manufacturing, facility-inspection or CMC findings are supplied.
PolyPid reports priority-review acceptance and a November 28, 2026 target, replacing Q1 2027 guidance. Its report of no filing issues does not establish clinical or CMC clearance.
